silhouette.reason: Fusiform body, tall sickle second dorsal and anal fins, yellow finlet rows, short pectorals and a crescent tail: names a bluefin tuna in SIDE and TOP at once.
fixes: make the caudal keels visible as a ridge on the tail stock in SIDE/TOP (fins.ts)

proportions.reason: 2.1 × 0.6 × 1.1 m for a 2 m fork length; body depth, fin positions and finlet count look right beside the dossier photos.
fixes: check the pectoral length against a side photo (it reads slightly long for Thunnus thynnus)

materials.reason: Metallic blue back with a strong highlight over a silver flank, yellow finlets and fin bases; the silver flank reads as flat grey paint rather than mirror-like scales.
fixes: raise metalness / lower roughness on the flank so it reflects like a fish side
iridescent band and faint silver spots/bars on the lower flank

detail.reason: Operculum line, eye with ring, finlets, lateral bars; but the body is a smooth shell (no lateral line, no corselet scale patch) and the fins are flat plates with no rays.
fixes: fin rays as shallow grooves on the dorsal, anal and caudal fins (fins.ts)
lateral line and corselet scale patch behind the head
gill slit depth at the operculum edge

wear.reason: Pristine: no frayed fin edges, no scratches, no slime sheen variation.
fixes: slightly frayed fin margins and a few scratches on the flank (seeded)

lod.reason: LOD2 (476 tris) keeps the outline, fins and the blue-over-silver split, but the body is clearly faceted and the finlets thin out.
fixes: keep finlets at LOD2 as a single flat yellow strip per side
give LOD2 more rings around the body (~700 tris) so the faceting stops reading
LOD1 at 4k drops a lot from 32k: add an intermediate ring count so the LOD0→LOD1 switch is softer
